question: A Connecticut real estate license expires and is still not renewed as of the ninetieth day after its expiration date. Under Conn. Gen. Stat. § 20-314(f), what is the significance of that ninetieth day?
choice_a: The license is automatically and permanently revoked with no further recourse
choice_b: After that point, the former licensee may only be reinstated through the commission's or department's discretionary reinstatement process, rather than a routine late renewal
choice_c: The licensee must immediately cease using the designation "real estate broker" but may still practice as an unlicensed assistant
choice_d: The ninetieth day triggers automatic referral to the Attorney General for prosecution
explanation: Section 20-314(f) provides that "[a]ny license which expires and is not renewed on or before the ninetieth day following the expiration date of such license may be reinstated by the commission or department, in the commission's or department's discretion," provided the license has lapsed less than three years. The 90-day mark is the point at which a simple late renewal is no longer available and the statutory reinstatement process (with its attestation, fee, and CE conditions) applies instead.

question: A former Connecticut licensee applies to reinstate a real estate license that lapsed 14 months earlier. Which pairing correctly reflects the two possible paths under § 20-314(f), depending on whether the applicant worked in the profession in Connecticut while the license was lapsed?
choice_a: Both paths require the applicant to retake and pass the full state licensing examination regardless of whether they worked during the lapse
choice_b: Working during the lapse period has no statutory consequence as long as the license is reinstated within three years
choice_c: If the applicant did NOT work during the lapse, they need only attest to that, pay the current renewal fee, and complete the CE required for the preceding year; if they DID work during the lapse, they must instead pay all license and late fees owing for the entire lapse period and demonstrate completed CE
choice_d: An applicant who worked during the lapse is permanently barred from reinstatement and must wait the full three years to apply as a brand-new applicant
explanation: Section 20-314(f) sets out two distinct tracks: a former licensee who attests they did not work in the occupation while lapsed need only pay the current renewal fee and complete the preceding year's CE; one who did work while lapsed must instead "pay all license and late fees due and owing for the lapse period and demonstrate that such applicant has completed all continuing education required for such license for the year preceding such reinstatement."

question: Under Conn. Gen. Stat. § 20-314(f), when a former licensee who worked during a lapse period seeks reinstatement, late fees are assessed for each year or fraction of a year of lapse. What are the correct late-fee amounts?
choice_a: $285 for each broker license and $375 for each salesperson license
choice_b: A flat $500 regardless of license type
choice_c: $120 for each broker license and $80 for each salesperson license
choice_d: $375 for each broker license and $285 for each salesperson license
explanation: The statute assesses late fees of "three hundred seventy-five dollars" for each real estate broker's license and "two hundred eighty-five dollars" for each real estate salesperson's license, for each year or fraction thereof of lapse.

question: Once reinstated under Conn. Gen. Stat. § 20-314(f), a reinstated real estate BROKER license and a reinstated real estate SALESPERSON license will next expire on which dates, respectively?
choice_a: Broker: next succeeding November 30; Salesperson: next succeeding May 31
choice_b: Both expire on the next succeeding November 30
choice_c: Broker: next succeeding May 31; Salesperson: next succeeding November 30
choice_d: Both expire exactly two years from the date of reinstatement
explanation: Section 20-314(f) states: "Any such reinstated broker's license shall expire on the next succeeding November thirtieth. Any such reinstated real estate salesperson's license shall expire on the next succeeding May thirty-first." Broker and salesperson licenses are on offset renewal cycles.

question: Under Conn. Gen. Stat. § 20-312(b), which of the following is NOT one of the statutory conditions that must be satisfied for a business entity to engage in the real estate business in Connecticut?
choice_a: A material part of the business entity's business must include engaging in the real estate business
choice_b: The business entity must maintain a minimum of $1,000,000 in professional liability (errors and omissions) insurance
choice_c: The entity's personnel who engage in the real estate business must be licensed, or exempt from licensure, under Chapter 392
choice_d: The business entity itself must have been issued a real estate broker license
explanation: Section 20-312(b) conditions engaging in the real estate business as a business entity on: (1) a material part of its business being the real estate business, (2) its real-estate personnel being licensed or exempt, (3) the entity itself holding a real estate broker license, (4) payment of the license/renewal fee under § 20-314, and (5) meeting the entity-type ownership structure in subdivision (5). There is no separate statutory minimum-insurance condition in this section.

question: Under Conn. Gen. Stat. § 20-312(b)(5), which type of business entity is EXEMPT from the requirement that licensed (or exempt) real estate brokers own or control at least 51% of the entity in order for the entity to hold a Connecticut real estate broker license?
choice_b: A general partnership with only two partners
explanation: Section 20-312(b)(5) provides that the entity ownership condition is met if "[t]he business entity is a publicly traded corporation or, if the business entity is not a publicly traded corporation" it meets one of the listed 51% broker-ownership/control tests for stock corporations, nonstock corporations, LLCs, or partnerships. Publicly traded corporations are carved out of the 51% test entirely.

question: For a Connecticut real estate broker business entity that is NOT publicly traded, § 20-312(b)(5) requires licensed (or exempt) real estate brokers to hold at least 51% of a specific measure that varies by entity type. Which pairing is correct?
choice_a: Stock corporation → board seats; nonstock corporation → issued shares; LLC → managers; partnership/LLP → capital contributions only
choice_b: All entity types are measured solely by number of licensed employees, not ownership interest
choice_c: Stock corporation → members; nonstock corporation → issued shares; LLC → partnership interest; partnership/LLP → LLC interest
choice_d: Stock corporation → issued shares; nonstock corporation → members; LLC → LLC ownership/control interest; partnership/LLP → partnership interest
explanation: Section 20-312(b)(5)(A)-(D) ties the 51% broker-ownership/control requirement to a different metric for each entity type: 51%+ of "total issued shares" for a stock corporation, 51%+ of the "members" for a nonstock corporation, 51%+ of the "interest in the limited liability company" for an LLC, and 51%+ of the "total partnership interest" for a partnership or LLP.

question: Under Conn. Gen. Stat. § 20-312(c), a business entity seeking or holding a Connecticut real estate broker license must file with the commission or department the identity and contact information of:
choice_b: Every licensed salesperson who is ever affiliated with the entity
choice_c: The entity's registered agent for service of process only
choice_d: All individuals owning any ownership interest in the entity, however small
explanation: Section 20-312(c) requires the business entity to "file with the commission, in a form and manner prescribed by the department, the identity of, and contact information for, at least one designated broker."

question: If a licensed Connecticut real estate business entity changes its designated broker, § 20-312(c) requires the entity to notify the commission of the change within how many days after the change becomes effective?
explanation: Section 20-312(c) states the business entity "shall notify the commission of any change in the identity of, or contact information for, such designated broker not later than thirty days after such change becomes effective." (This is distinct from the separate 14-calendar-day notice an associate broker must give the department after a supervising-licensee affiliation terminates under § 20-312c(c).)

question: Once a business entity has been issued a real estate broker license under § 20-312, what does § 20-314(f) say about the entity's designated broker?
choice_a: The designated broker must obtain and pay for a second, separate individual broker license before acting on the entity's behalf
choice_b: The designated broker may not personally engage in real estate transactions and may only administratively supervise
choice_c: The designated broker may, upon compliance with Chapter 392 and without payment of any further fee, perform all of the acts of a real estate broker on behalf of the business entity
choice_d: The designated broker's authority automatically expires after one year and must be renewed annually
explanation: Section 20-314(f) provides that "[a] real estate broker's license issued to any business entity shall entitle the designated broker, upon compliance with the terms of this chapter, but without the payment of any further fee, to perform all of the acts of a real estate broker under this chapter on behalf of such business entity."

question: How does Conn. Gen. Stat. § 20-311 define a "designated broker"?
choice_a: Any salesperson chosen by majority vote of a brokerage's agents to represent them at commission meetings
choice_b: A purely honorary title carrying no supervisory authority or legal significance
choice_c: The broker within a firm who has held a license the longest
choice_d: The individual real estate broker whom a real estate broker business entity names as the individual broker responsible for the supervision and overall operation of such business entity's engagement in the real estate business in Connecticut
explanation: Section 20-311 defines "designated broker" as "the individual real estate broker whom a real estate broker business entity names as the individual broker responsible for the supervision and overall operation of such business entity's engagement in the real estate business in this state." This is a distinct defined term from "supervising licensee."

question: Under Conn. Gen. Stat. § 20-312(d), what is the maximum fine the Real Estate Commission may impose per violation on a person who engages in the real estate business — including leasing or rental activity — without the license required by § 20-312?
explanation: Section 20-312(d) authorizes the commission to "impose a fine of not more than five thousand dollars per violation on any person that engages in the real estate business, including, but not limited to, leasing or rental activity, without a license required by this section."

question: Under Conn. Gen. Stat. § 20-312c(a), an associate broker may lawfully engage in the real estate business only if the supervising licensee:
choice_a: Has filed a formal written supervision plan with the Department of Consumer Protection
choice_b: Knows that the associate broker is engaging in the real estate business AND has consented to the associate broker doing so
choice_c: Is physically present in the office at the time of every transaction
choice_d: Has personally co-signed every listing and purchase agreement the associate broker prepares
explanation: Section 20-312c(a) provides that "[n]o associate broker shall engage in the real estate business unless the supervising licensee that is responsible for controlling and supervising the associate broker (1) knows that such associate broker is engaging in the real estate business, and (2) has consented to such associate broker engaging in the real estate business." Both knowledge and consent are required.

question: Under Conn. Gen. Stat. § 20-312c(b), a supervising licensee's responsibility for the actions of an associate broker under that supervising licensee's control is:
choice_a: Nonexistent, because an associate broker already holds a full broker's license and is presumed capable of self-supervision
choice_b: Automatically capped at $10,000 per transaction by statute
choice_c: The same extent of responsibility the supervising licensee would bear if that associate broker were instead a real estate salesperson affiliated with the supervising licensee
choice_d: Limited to acts the supervising licensee personally witnessed or pre-approved in writing
explanation: Section 20-312c(b) states: "Each supervising licensee shall be responsible for the actions of the associate brokers who are under such supervising licensee's control and supervision to the same extent that such supervising licensee would be responsible for such associate brokers if such associate brokers were real estate salespersons affiliated with such supervising licensee." The fact that an associate broker is broker-licensed does not reduce the supervising licensee's exposure.

question: If an associate broker's affiliation with a supervising licensee is terminated, § 20-312c(c) requires the associate broker to notify the Department of Consumer Protection of the termination within how many calendar days of the termination (or of affiliating with a new supervising licensee, whichever occurs first)?
explanation: Section 20-312c(c) provides: "If an associate broker's affiliation with a supervising licensee is terminated, the associate broker shall notify the department of such termination not later than fourteen calendar days after such termination or such associate broker's affiliation with another supervising licensee, whichever occurs first."

question: Under Conn. Gen. Stat. § 20-312c(d), advertisements placed by an associate broker must:
choice_a: Comply with all advertising requirements and standards that apply to real estate brokers, and prominently include the name of the supervising licensee who controls and supervises the associate broker
choice_b: Omit any reference to a supervising broker so as not to confuse consumers about who the licensee is
choice_c: Be pre-approved in writing by the Real Estate Commission before each publication
choice_d: List only the associate broker's individual license number and no other identifying information
explanation: Section 20-312c(d) requires that "[e]ach associate broker shall comply with all advertising requirements and standards that apply to real estate brokers, and shall include the name of the supervising licensee who controls and supervises such associate broker at a prominent location in all of such associate broker's advertisements."

question: Under Conn. Gen. Stat. § 20-311, how is an "associate broker" defined, and how does that differ from an ordinary real estate salesperson?
choice_a: An associate broker is simply a first-year salesperson working under a mentor, with no distinct licensure
choice_b: An associate broker is a real estate broker who is affiliated with, or employed by, a supervising licensee as an independent contractor or employee and has the authority to engage in the real estate business on behalf of that supervising licensee — unlike a salesperson, an associate broker already holds broker-level licensure
choice_c: An associate broker is an unlicensed office administrator who coordinates listings for a brokerage
choice_d: An associate broker and a real estate salesperson are legally identical terms for the same license type
explanation: Section 20-311 defines an "associate broker" as a real estate broker who (A) is affiliated with a supervising licensee as an independent contractor or employed by a supervising licensee, and (B) has the authority to engage in the real estate business on behalf of such supervising licensee. Unlike a salesperson, an associate broker holds broker-level licensure but still operates under a supervising licensee's control, which is why § 20-312c imposes specific consent, liability, notice, and advertising rules on that relationship.
